summary: This paper introduces LOCOMO, a benchmark and evaluation framework for very long-term conversational memory in LLM agents, covering multi-session dialogue, event summarization, and multimodal response generation.
why_it_matters: It is a foundational evaluation asset for the vault because later memory papers such as Mem0 and SimpleMem use LoCoMo to argue that their systems actually improve long-horizon conversational memory.
method_setup: The paper builds persona-driven, multi-session dialogues grounded in event graphs, evaluates models on question answering, event summarization, and multimodal dialogue generation, and compares long-context and retrieval-augmented approaches using raw dialogue history, observations, and summaries.
key_claims: Existing LLM agents remain far from human-level performance on very long-term conversational memory.
Observation-based retrieval works better than retrieving raw dialogue history for long-horizon memory tasks.
Temporal reasoning and adversarial questions remain particularly difficult for current memory-augmented systems.
limitations: Longer context windows alone do not solve long-term conversational memory.
Current models still hallucinate and struggle with temporally grounded reasoning over many sessions.
Standard text-generation metrics are insufficient for fully capturing conversational memory quality.
builds_on_unresolved: Conversation Chronicles: Towards Diverse Temporal and Relational Dynamics in Multi-Session Conversations
Beyond Goldfish Memory: Long-Term Open-Domain Conversation
Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
